name: Scapular Pull-Up
definition: A strict bilateral suspended repetition performed from a closed pronated grip on a horizontal pull-up bar with unsupported feet and fully extended elbows. Each repetition begins with the scapulae naturally elevated, pulls them down and back so the straight-arm body rises slightly, pauses briefly at the source-explicit endpoint, and returns under control to naturally elevated suspension. Shoulder-width grip and no deliberate swing are conservative catalog narrowings rather than reported Army or LA County measurements. The source-exact prime signature combines scapular depression and retraction; gravity also tends to open the fingers throughout the set. Lower-trapezius, grip, and support-chain roles are anatomy-and-mechanics inferences rather than exact-fixture muscle rankings. Active and Passive Dead Hangs, full Pull-Ups, flexed-arm holds, kipping, weighted or assisted variants, climbing-edge hangs, and depression without retraction remain outside this narrow contract.

execution.startingPosition: Take a shoulder-width closed overhand grip on a horizontal pull-up bar, fully extend both elbows, lift the feet clear of the floor, and let the shoulder blades rise naturally.
execution.movement: Keep both elbows straight and pull both shoulder blades down and back so the body rises slightly without swinging.
execution.endpoint: Finish with the shoulders away from the ears and the shoulder blades drawn down and back, then pause briefly without inventing a timed hold.
execution.returnPhase: Return under control until the shoulder blades are naturally elevated again before starting the next repetition.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep both elbows fully extended and do not add shoulder or elbow pulling motion.
execution.supportAndPosture: Support the full bodyweight through both hands with no foot assistance, kipping, or leg swing.
disqualifyingCompensations: Holding the down-and-back position for time turns the exercise into an Active Dead Hang.
Bending the elbows or pulling the chest toward the bar turns it into a Pull-Up.
Using hip or leg swing turns it into a kipping variation.
